scope: Reader-experience and PDF/print UX opportunities in latest close-readings editions; sampled full-size visual review, bookmark/metadata inspection and bounded builder reading. No edits, new art, build, browser or publication.

findings.finding: Each page contains only two continuation lines, starting mid-sentence (Manglu; cinema-music). Actual pixels inspected. These are pagination fragments, not breathing space.
findings.recommendation: Recover the lines on the preceding page through bounded spacing or group the final paragraph coherently. Do not commission art to disguise these leaves.

findings.finding: Complete square author portrait and simple caption occupy p8; title, part introduction and prose start p9. Builder explicitly inserts a portrait leaf when image/title/intro exceed its opener-height threshold. This is deliberate frontispiece behavior, not an accidental missing title.
findings.recommendation: Prefer retaining the uncropped full portrait as a facing frontispiece in print: p8 left, p9 opening right. For digital, consider a smaller complete portrait integrated with heading and first paragraph, using a fit calculation rather than a fixed oversized frame. If the user values the full-width portrait more, retain p8 deliberately; do not fill its lower blank area with unrelated art.

findings.finding: Bijay Mohanty ends with a five-line onward-link paragraph on its own page; Sabyasachi ends with a heading and three-line reflection. Both are coherent but visually disproportionately sparse.
findings.recommendation: First try keeping the closing section with prior narrative. Only if a deliberate ending page is retained, consider one modest scene-relevant conceptual vignette; it must not reconstruct a named person or historical event. Art is secondary to paragraph flow.

findings.finding: Existing threshold, publicity-sheet and chair drawings provide distinct, relevant endings with aligned, readable captions. They occupy usable space without creating a new leaf.
findings.recommendation: Keep these as the model: select a small number of thematic endings, retain white margins and never force a drawing into every chapter. Do not enlarge art merely to consume remaining white space.

findings.finding: OTT ends with provider links and a short question about returns to makers; a large lower area is empty. It is a coherent transition into economics, not a broken paragraph.
findings.recommendation: Optional candidate for a restrained image connecting a screen and the people/work behind it, if it contributes a fresh idea. Leaving this pause unillustrated is equally defensible; do not use a generic decorative device or add a page.

findings.pages: digital 3–7; print contents and p7 inspected by extraction
findings.finding: Four contents pages precede the useful ten-reading path on p7. The short path reduces the apparent obligation to finish fifty chapters, but readers encounter the long inventory first.
findings.recommendation: Consider placing the ten-reading invitation before the full contents or give it a prominent opening-page signpost. Preserve the complete contents and working chapter/page links. Existing hierarchy is clear; this is a discoverability improvement, not a broken route.

findings.finding: Ordinary numbered notes combine source and image credits successfully. Print still shows repeated Return text, which is useful digitally but not actionable on paper; S codes then require a second lookup in a long URL directory.
findings.recommendation: In print, consider replacing Return with source-page references or omitting that digital action label. Offer one stable online source directory address/optional QR as a convenience while retaining citations and essential printed addresses; no automatic shortening that loses provenance. Keep clickable note/return behavior digitally.

findings.finding: Title, author and document language en are present; bookmark destinations are valid. Neither PDF has a StructTreeRoot or MarkInfo. Thus headings, reading order, figures/alt text, tables and language changes are not provided as a tagged semantic structure.
findings.recommendation: Treat accessible digital reading as separate substantive work: real semantic tags, language spans including Odia, meaningful figure alternatives, logical reading order and assistive-technology testing. Do not set Marked alone or claim PDF/UA. Existing HTML may remain the practical reading alternative.

preferred_direction: Fix true pagination fragments before adding illustrations. Preserve the full portrait and let print use it as an intentional frontispiece; choose a more compact uncropped digital opener only if desired. Use occasional story-specific closing drawings, not an automatic end-of-chapter decoration system.
limitations: Not an all-page fresh proof; selected pages explicitly listed. Maya ending pixels were also inspected in immediately preceding bounded review of these exact hashes.
No screen-reader or print binding test performed; print-facing-page recommendation assumes conventional odd-right pagination.
No PDF/UA or press-ready certification; typography/accessibility improvements are proposals only.
